name: Spinal Dysraphism with a Posterior Meningocele

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Spinal Dysraphism with Posterior Meningocele

criteria.description: Presence of a cystic, skin-covered sac protruding from the posterior midline of the spine
MRI or ultrasound demonstrating herniation of meninges through a vertebral defect without neural tissue involvement
Neurological examination showing intact motor and sensory function in most cases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a posterior midline cystic sac with imaging confirmation of meningeal herniation without neural tissue involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from myelomeningocele is critical; neurological deficits are typically absent or mild.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Posterior midline cystic sac covered by intact skin
pathognomonic.notes: Typically located in the lumbosacral region

pathognomonic.symptomName: Vertebral arch defect underlying the meningocele
searchTerms: gap in vertebral arch near lesion

common.symptomName: Normal or near-normal lower limb motor function

common.notes: May present as urinary urgency or incontinence

common.symptomName: Cutaneous stigmata overlying the lesion (e.g., hair tuft, skin dimple)
searchTerms: skin signs over lesion like hair tuft
skin dimple or hairy patch on lesion
visible skin marks on affected area

occasional.notes: Including back pain and leg weakness
May develop secondary to neurological involvement

rare.symptomName: Infection of the meningocele sac (meningitis or abscess)

laboratory: CSF analysis if sac rupture suspected
imaging: MRI demonstrating meningeal sac herniation through vertebral defect without neural tissue
Ultrasound useful in neonates for spinal defect visualization
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; multifactorial etiology suspected
other: Physical examination revealing cystic sac covered by intact skin
Neurological assessment typically normal or mildly affected

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of neural tissue within the sac
No external sac or cystic protrusion
Only vertebral defect without meningeal herniation

redFlags: Rapid enlargement or rupture of the meningocele sac
Signs of infection such as fever or sac erythema
Progressive neurological deficits including weakness or sensory loss
references: Kumar R, et al. Spinal Dysraphism: Clinical and Radiological Features. Neurol India. 2020.
Orphanet Report on Spinal Dysraphism with Posterior Meningocele, ORPHA:268744.
